Photograph: Michael Steele/Getty Images Championship Championship roundup: West Ham stage dramatic comeback on Scott Parker’s opening night
 West Ham recover from 3-0 down to draw 3-3 at Cardiff
 Leaders Middlesbrough beaten 2-0 at Wrexham
 Guardian sport Wed 4 Nov 2026 17.18 EST Last modified on Wed 4 Nov 2026 17.20 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Scott Parker’s return to West Ham had had looked like beginning in painful fashion but instead featured a stunning comeback from 3-0 down. The east London club’s new head coach had watched Cardiff ’s Jack Moylan help himself to a first-half hat-trick, before a rousing response after the break ended with Max Kilman levelling the scores at 3-3 eight minutes from time. Elsewhere in the Championship, leaders Middlesbrough went down 2-0 at Wrexham .
 Parker had been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach earlier on Wednesday, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday. The club’s former midfielder was appointed on a two-and-a-half year contract.
 West Ham confirm Scott Parker as head coach after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo Read more Moylan halted the initial feelgood factor among the visiting support in the 11th minute at Cardiff City Stadium. His right-foot drive from the tip of the D left visiting goalkeeper Mads Hermansen helpless as it sped into the top left corner. Moylan was then brought down for a penalty – the Ireland midfielder got up to spank it home to the left as Hermansen dived right in the 37th minute.
 Within two minutes, Will Fish thought he had turned in a corner for Cardiff’s third – the centre-back deftly headed towards goal, but Moylan was directly behind him and claimed his hat-trick after making the final touch.
 After the break, a completely different story. Divine Mukasa reduced the deficit in the 58th minute, finishing calmly over the stranded Nathan Trott after a fine ball over the top from Jarrod Bowen, before Arne Engels capitalised on a mix-up in the home defence to make it 3-2.
 In the 82nd minute, Bowen was again the supplier, curling in an inviting cross from the right that was turned in by centre-back Kilman to make it 3-3 from close range.
 At the Racecourse, Wrexham waited until the 70th minute to break the deadlock against Middlesbrough, before George Thomason smashed a shot into the ground from just outside the area, which rocketed past a crowd of defenders and through the unsighted visiting goalkeeper Radek Vítek. Oli Rathbone then made it 2-0 in the 84th minute.

 Scott Twine scored a stunning, curling free-kick to give Bristol City the lead at Ashton Gate but promotion-chasing Wolves turned the match around with two late goals from Sean Neave to make it a 2-1 win to the visitors. Neave, on loan from Newcastle, came off the bench to score on 82 and 89 minutes to win it for the visitors.
